subject: All Subjects
summary: a final one-stop formula sheet across the whole syllabus — every solution opens with the formula it uses: permutations with repeated letters, eigenvalue sum and product, Newton–Raphson, restitution, principal stresses, Euler's effective lengths, piston acceleration, transmissibility, fillet-weld throat, pump power and affinity laws, lumped cooling, ideal-gas entropy change, Merchant's shear angle and the M/M/1 queue

questions.text: The number of distinct arrangements of all the letters of the word ENGINEER is ______
solution: Formula: Arrangements of n objects with p, q, … identical = n!/(p! q! …).
Concept: ENGINEER has 8 letters: E three times, N twice, G, I and R once each.
Exam tip: Related formulas: circular arrangements of n distinct objects (n − 1)!; selections nCr = n!/[r!(n − r)!]; arrangements nPr = n!/(n − r)!.

questions.text: A 3 × 3 matrix A has trace 10, and two of its eigenvalues are 2 and 3. The determinant of A is
solution: Formula: Σλi = trace A (sum of diagonal entries); Πλi = det A.
Concept: The third eigenvalue follows from the trace, and then the determinant is the product of all three.
Exam tip: Eigenvalues of A−1, Ak, A + cI and kA are 1/λ, λk, λ + c and kλ; eigenvalues of a triangular matrix are its diagonal entries.

questions.text: A root of x³ − 2x − 5 = 0 is found by the Newton–Raphson method starting from x<sub>0</sub> = 2. The first iterate x<sub>1</sub> (round off to 2 decimal places) is ______
solution: Formula: xn+1 = xn − f(xn)/f′(xn).
Concept: f(x) = x³ − 2x − 5 and f′(x) = 3x² − 2.

Exam tip: NR converges quadratically for a simple root. Bisection halves the interval each step; regula falsi uses x = (a f(b) − b f(a))/(f(b) − f(a)); the secant method uses the same formula with the two latest points.

questions.text: A ball is dropped from a height of 8 m onto a hard floor. The coefficient of restitution between the ball and the floor is 0.5. The height reached by the ball after its second bounce is
solution: Formula: e = (velocity of separation)/(velocity of approach); for a ball dropped from h, the rebound height after n bounces is hn = e2nh.
Concept: Each impact multiplies the speed by e, and the height (∝ v²) by e².
Exam tip: After the first bounce the height is e²h = 2 m. Linear momentum is conserved in a collision of two free bodies; kinetic energy is conserved only if e = 1.

questions.text: At a point in plane stress, σ<sub>x</sub> = 50 MPa (tension), σ<sub>y</sub> = 10 MPa (compression) and τ<sub>xy</sub> = 40 MPa. The principal stresses are
solution: Formula: σ1,2 = (σx + σy)/2 ± √{[(σx − σy)/2]² + τxy²}; tan 2θp = 2τxy/(σx − σy).
Concept: The centre of Mohr's circle is at the mean normal stress and its radius equals the maximum in-plane shear stress.
Exam tip: Check: σ1 + σ2 = σx + σy = 40 MPa (first stress invariant). Maximum in-plane shear = radius = 50 MPa.

questions.text: A solid circular steel strut of 40 mm diameter and 2.5 m length is fixed at one end and pinned at the other. Taking E = 200 GPa, its Euler buckling load (in kN) is ______ (round off to 1 decimal place)
solution: Formula: Pcr = π²EI/Le²; Le = L (both ends pinned), 2L (fixed–free), L/2 (both fixed), L/√2 (fixed–pinned).
Concept: For a solid circle I = πd⁴/64 = π × 40⁴/64 = 1.257 × 10⁵ mm⁴.
Exam tip: Relative to both ends pinned, the buckling loads are in the ratio 1/4 (fixed–free) : 1 : 2 (fixed–pinned) : 4 (both fixed). Slenderness ratio = Le/k with k = √(I/A).

questions.text: In a slider–crank mechanism the crank is 50 mm long, the connecting rod is 200 mm long and the crank turns uniformly at 100 rad/s. The acceleration of the piston when the crank is at inner dead centre (θ = 0°) is
solution: Formula: ap ≈ rω²[cos θ + (cos 2θ)/n], with n = l/r; piston velocity vp ≈ rω[sin θ + (sin 2θ)/(2n)].
Concept: n = 200/50 = 4 and rω² = 0.05 × 100² = 500 m/s².
At θ = 0°: ap = 500(1 + 1/4) = 625 m/s² (C); at outer dead centre (θ = 180°) it is 500(1 − 1/4) = 375 m/s².
Exam tip: The inertia force of the reciprocating mass m is F = m ap; its primary part is mrω² cos θ and its secondary part mrω² cos 2θ/n.

questions.text: An undamped machine mounting runs at three times its natural frequency. The force transmissibility is
solution: Formula: TR = √[1 + (2ζr)²]/√[(1 − r²)² + (2ζr)²], with r = ω/ωn; for ζ = 0, TR = 1/|1 − r²|.
Concept: Isolation (TR < 1) needs r > √2.
TR = 1/|1 − 9| = 1/8 = 0.125 (B); i.e. 12.5 % of the force reaches the foundation.
Exam tip: For r > √2, adding damping increases TR. Magnification factor (amplitude) X/Xst = 1/√[(1 − r²)² + (2ζr)²], which for ζ = 0 has the same value here.

questions.text: Two plates are joined by fillet welds of 8 mm leg size with a total weld length of 150 mm. The permissible shear stress in the weld is 90 MPa. The safe load the joint can carry (in kN) is ______ (round off to 2 decimal places)
solution: Formula: Fillet-weld strength P = τ × t × L, where the throat thickness t = s cos 45° = 0.707s.
Concept: Fillet welds fail in shear across the throat, the smallest section of the weld.
Exam tip: Using the leg size s instead of the throat (108 kN) is the classic error. For a butt weld P = σ t L with t = plate thickness.

questions.text: A pump delivers 0.05 m³/s of water against a total head of 40 m. Its overall efficiency is 75 %. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², the power required to drive the pump (in kW) is ______ (round off to 2 decimal places)
solution: Formula: Water (hydraulic) power = ρgQH; shaft power = ρgQH/η for a pump (and ηρgQH for a turbine).
Exam tip: Divide by η for a pump (input is larger) and multiply for a turbine (output is smaller). Pump specific speed Ns = N√Q/H3/4; turbine Ns = N√P/H5/4.

questions.text: The speed of a centrifugal pump is doubled (same impeller, same fluid, similar operating point). Its discharge, head and power become, respectively,
solution: Formula: Affinity laws for one pump: Q ∝ N, H ∝ N², P ∝ N³ (for a changed impeller size at the same N: Q ∝ D³, H ∝ D², P ∝ D⁵).
Concept: Similar velocity triangles: all velocities scale with N, so Q ∝ N, H ∝ (velocity)² ∝ N², P ∝ QH ∝ N³.
Doubling N: Q × 2, H × 4, P × 8: (A).
Exam tip: General scaling: Q/(ND³), gH/(N²D²) and P/(ρN³D⁵) stay constant between geometrically similar machines.

questions.text: A small metal sphere at 200 °C is suddenly placed in a fluid at 20 °C. Lumped analysis applies. Its temperature (in °C) after a time equal to two time constants is ______ (round off to 2 decimal places)
solution: Formula: (T − T∞)/(Ti − T∞) = e−t/τ, with time constant τ = ρcV/(hA); valid when Bi = hLc/k < 0.1, Lc = V/A.
Concept: After t = 2τ the excess temperature falls to e−2 = 0.1353 of its initial value.
Exam tip: After one time constant 36.8 % of the initial excess remains (63.2 % of the change is complete). Lc = r/3 for a sphere, r/2 for a long cylinder, half-thickness for a plate.

questions.text: Air (c<sub>p</sub> = 1.005 kJ/kg·K, R = 0.287 kJ/kg·K) goes from 1 bar and 300 K to 3 bar and 500 K. Its specific entropy change is about
solution: Formula: Δs = cp ln(T2/T1) − R ln(p2/p1) = cv ln(T2/T1) + R ln(v2/v1).
Concept: Entropy is a property, so Δs depends only on the end states and not on the path.
Exam tip: A pressure rise lowers entropy, so the R ln(p2/p1) term is subtracted; adding it gives 0.828. For an incompressible solid or liquid, Δs = c ln(T2/T1).

questions.text: In orthogonal cutting with a tool of rake angle 8°, the friction angle at the tool–chip interface is 36°. The shear angle given by Merchant's theory is
solution: Formula: Merchant: 2φ + β − α = 90°, i.e. φ = 45° + α/2 − β/2. Also tan φ = r cos α/(1 − r sin α), with chip thickness ratio r = t/tc.
Concept: Merchant assumed that the shear plane sets itself where the cutting energy is minimum.
Exam tip: A larger rake angle or a smaller friction angle gives a larger shear angle, a thinner chip and a lower cutting force. Shear strain γ = cot φ + tan(φ − α).

questions.text: Trucks arrive at a single loading bay in a Poisson stream at 15 per hour, and the loading time is exponential with a mean rate of 20 per hour (M/M/1). The average time a truck waits in the queue before loading starts (in minutes) is ______
solution: Formula: For M/M/1 with ρ = λ/μ: Ls = λ/(μ − λ), Lq = λ²/[μ(μ − λ)], Ws = 1/(μ − λ), Wq = λ/[μ(μ − λ)]; Little's law L = λW.
Concept: ρ = 15/20 = 0.75 < 1, so the queue is stable.
Wq = 15/(20 × 5) = 0.15 h = 9 minutes (Ws = 1/5 h = 12 min, Lq = 2.25 trucks).
Exam tip: Ws − Wq = 1/μ, the mean service time (3 min here). The probability that the bay is idle is 1 − ρ = 0.25.
